newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: INTERVIEW-Jade Technologies sees better year ahead.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Jade Technologies sees better year ahead.

text.p: U.S. Industries Inc (USI)'s subsidiary, Jade Technolgies Singapore Ltd, should see a better 1997 on the back of a brighter outlook for the global electronics industry, company officials said on Wednesday.
"Jade Technologies should see better earnings and sales performance this year," said managing director Peter Kalmarczie in an interview with Reuters.
The company produces leadframes or conduits for transmitting electronic signals -- a crucial part of a semiconductor.
The improved outlook was fuelled by expectations of a turnaround in the sluggish global electronics industry, reflected by the better U.S. book-to-bill ratio, said company director Brian Beazer.
The U.S. book-to-bill ratio, often used to gauge demand for memory chips, has been improving since the fourth quarter of 1996. It compares product orders to shipments during a month.
Jade Technologies saw pre-tax profit for fiscal year 1996 at Singapore $2.569 million against S$2.422 million in 1995 while turnover slipped to S$24.95 million in 1996 from S$30 million previously.
The drop in turnover was attributed mainly to the slowdown in the global electronics industry.
Kalmarczie said the company was expanding its capacity in its 5,276 square metre Singapore plant through the adoption of a new technology, etching.
The company expects this S$5.5 million technology investment to bolster turnover and profit margins.
"A new project to expand existing building and go into etching of leadframes will improve margins and lead us into areas that we are currently not involved," Kalmarczie said.
Leadframe etching, said Kalmarczie, would allow the company to move from using metal stampers to make leadframes to using acid to burn.

Kalmarczie said etching would see the company capture new customers -- those who seek the higher-quality leadframes like integrated circuits (IC) leadframes, as well as those in the development stages who require only small volumes of leadframes.
IC leadframes function as electrical connections between silicon wafer chips and the printed circuit board.
The company expects total plant capacity of over two billion leadframes to be enhanced by six percent with etching while production of IC leadframes would rise by 12 percent.

Jade Technologies is planning to list about 25 percent of its total issued share capital on the Stock Exchange of Singapore in the next week or two, said president and chief operating officer of USI, John Raos.
Raos said the listing of Jade Technologies would be the American consumer and building products company's first venture into South East Asia's equity market.
After the public listing of Jade Technologies's shares, USI would continue to own 75 percent of the leadframe manufacturing company.
Raos said the proceeds from the initial public offering would be used by Jade Technologies in its etching investment and as working capital.
